title: Protocol for generating a mouse model of gastric MALT lymphoma and the identification of MALT lymphoma cell populations by immunostaining
protocol: Sacrifice all mice through cervical dislocation under anesthesia.
Resect the stomachs, opening at the outer curvature.
Free half of the stomach in cryo-embedding compound (O.C.T).
Set the inside temperature of the device between −15°C and −20°C.
Slice the tissue to create 10-μm thick sections.
Immediately place the tissue sections in a staining vat containing 200 mL of acetone for about 1 s.
Dry the sections using an air dryer.
Store the sections at −30°C until staining.
Air dry the tissue sections for 1–2 hours at room temperature.
Fix the sections in acetone for 5–10 minutes inside a chemical hood.
Wash the sections in 1× PBS for 3 minutes.
Repeat the wash with 1× PBS twice more.
Remove excess 1× PBS from the section using a wipe.
Add 100 mL of 10% goat serum drop-wise onto the section and incubate for 30 minutes in a humid chamber for blocking.
Wash the sections thrice with PBS, each for 3 minutes.
After removing excess 1× PBS, add 100 μL of primary antibody (diluted 1:20–50 with 1× PBS) drop-wise and incubate at room temperature for 2 hours or at 4°C for 12–24 hours in a humid chamber.
Wash the sections thrice with 1× PBS, each for 3 minutes.
Remove excess 1× PBS from the section.
Add 100 μL of secondary antibody (diluted in 1× PBS) drop-wise and incubate at room temperature for 1 hour in a dark room in a humid chamber.
Wash the sections thrice with 1× PBS, each for 3 minutes.
Remove excess 1× PBS from the section.
Add 100 μL of fluorescent mounting medium drop-wise onto the tissue section.
Cover the tissue section with a coverslip (size: 24 × 32 mm).
Aspirate any air bubbles in the sample using a PIPETMAN® pipetman.
Store the encapsulated mounting medium at 4°C for up to 2-3 days.
Observe fluorescence signals under a confocal laser-scanning microscope.
Use suitable software, such as LSM Image Browser, to analyze the images.
Set the pixels in the x-y plane to 1024 × 1024 pixels at a pixel size of 0.83 μm/pixel.
